answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with progressive trust ceilings and refundable bonds: each new identity starts with a tiny transaction limit and a deposit that grows with the volume it handles. To forge a plume of fake identities is costly: every fake needs its own locked deposit plus a long history of attested work before its ceiling lifts, while one honest identity builds reputation cheaply. Once an identity earns a saffron trust tier from repeated verified completions, its bond requirement falls, so attackers pay lockup and time per fake while honest agents pay almost nothing.
